source.title: Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Sergeant at Arms is directed to make the proclamation.

turns.speaker: Alfredo Sotto Corpuz
turns.text: All persons are commanded to keep silent under pain of penalty while the Impeachment Court is in session for the trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte is hereby called to order. We shall be led in prayer by Senator-Judge JV Ejercito.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Amon namin mga pangyarihan, lumalapit kami sa iyo nang may pakumbaba. Batid namin na ang karunungan ng tao ay may hangganan. Ngunit ang iyong katotohanan at katarungan ay nanatili magpakailanman.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Sa

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: pagtupad namin ng aming tungkulin binang mga senator judges, hinihiling namin ang iyong gabay sa lahat ng aming gagawin. Pagkalooban mo, nawa kami ng tapat na puso at malinaw na pag-iisip. Sa buong panahon ng paglilitis na ito, Panginoon, nakikiusap po kami na kayo niyo kami sa landas na makatarungan na may patas na pagtingin sa karapatan ng bawat isa. Dalhin niyo kami sa liwanag pagkat nakapiring ang aming mga mata, hindi man po namin hiningi, ngunit ipinagkatiwala sa aming konstitusyon ang timbangan ng katarungan. Kumiling nawa ito sa karapat-dapat na pagkalooban nito. Nawa ang inyong salita ang maging gabays sa aming paglilingkod at pagdala sa amin sa katotohanan. Kagaya po ng Winika sa Leviticus 19.15, Do not pervert justice, do not show partiality, but judge your neighbor fairly. Lagi po naman tatandaan ang tagubili niyong ito. Amma, anuman ang maging bunga ng paglilitis na ito, hindi nawa itong makita bilang tagumpay ng isa at pagkatalo ng iba, kundi para sa kabubuti ng sambay ng Pilipino. Lahat po ng aming gagawin ay para sa kalulugod mo at hindi para sa kapinabangan ng sino mang tao, mga partido o kanilang mga pansariling interes. Kundi ito'y para sa pagpapatibay ng aming mainstitusyon ng pamalaan at sa pagpapanatili ng tiwala ng mamamayan sa demokrasya ng aming bayan. Bum puso po naming nananalangin na sa lahat ang aming gagawin, lagit-lagi naming kayong pinupuryan. Amen.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: are no objections, we dispense with the reading of the July 8, 2026 Journal of the Senate sitting as an impeachment court and consider the same as approved.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: 2026. In the matter of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Sen. Rafi Tulfo is seeking recognition. What is the pleasure of Sen. Judge Rafi Tulfo?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you, Presiding Judge Escudero. Short inquiry lang po for the defense, particularly kay Atty. Mark Vinluan. Atty., you know what? During the last hearing, when you delivered a manifestation in reply to the prosecution's statement regarding the fourth article of impeachment, You said, and I quote, The truth of the matter is this. She and her family were threatened, and while her response was unconventional, it was justified. What triggered her response was a question about Operation Romanov, which is the plot to eliminate VP Sara and her family. End of quote. Now, Atty. Bin Luan, this Operation Romanov that you mentioned, Are you referring to the Operation Romanov mentioned by the blogger Princess Maui during the online press conference of BP-SARA?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. So, the question was raised during the press conference by this Princess Maui, but I did not see her name as a list of defense witnesses in the pre-trial order. So, will you be presenting her as your witness?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, at this point, it will depend on... What will be established by the prosecution, the defense reserve its right to call or not call any witness depending on the course of the trial.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Oh, I see. Okay. So, in other words, will you also be presenting any other witness to prove this threat or this operation, Romanov?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. That will be part of our evidence in chief.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: May this court know now? Kung sino-sino itong mga witnesses na inyong i-present? Of course,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: of course, Your Honor. We are not at liberty to disclose that at this time. Again, it will depend on the course of the time.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Your Honors, Presiding Judge, the first time I've heard about this Romanov is during the Maisog Leaders Forum in Davao City. That was on January 28, 2024. Correct me if I'm wrong. It was mentioned by Mayor Baste Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: At that time, hindi ko alam anong ibig sabihin ng Romanov at sino mga ito. In fact, ginugil ko yan. Sino itong family Romanov? So napagalaman ko, apparently, they were the ruling family in Russia that was murdered by the Bolsheviks in the night of July 16, 1918. Malapit-lapit na sa anniversary, 108th anniversary. Kasi ano ba tayo ngayon, July 13. Anyway, may relasyon ba ito sa binanggit ni Bastet sa sinabi ni Princess Maui at yung binanggit mo? Nakakarelasyon ba yung tatlo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, I have no personal knowledge of what Mayor Bastet said so I cannot comment on that, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: So hindi mo napanood yun? No, Your

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay. And last question. What did you mean when you said that BP's arrest response was unconventional?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, it was a description, Your Honor, of the statements that she made during that press conference.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Why is it unconventional?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, the basic meaning of the word is, it will explain itself, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, that's all, Presiding Judge. Noted and entered into the records.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, what is the pleasure of the Honorable Defensor, one of the members of the panel of prosecutors. You may

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: proceed,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Sir.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honors. Your Honors, before we proceed, With the examination of our second witness, Your Honors, the prosecution is in receipt of a letter dated July 10, 2026 from NBI Director Melvin A. Matibag requesting that his testimony be scheduled or calendared at the earliest setting considering that the National Bureau of Investigation, Your Honors, has been invited by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. In coordination with the Royal Thai Police for a regional summit on scam center compounds and transnational organized crime. In that regard, Your Honor, the prosecution would like to request that the scheduled testimony of NBI Director Melvin Matibag be scheduled tomorrow after the testimony of our second witness, Atty. Jeremy A. Lotoc.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: After the testimony of your second witness.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Yes, your honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: But the supposed witness scheduled for tomorrow is Atty.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Zulaika Lopez for the gentleman's manifestation in the last hearing.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: That's correct, your honor. After we have dispensed with the testimony of NBI Director Matibag, we can proceed with the schedule of witnesses as provided in the list to the senator judges last week, your honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: To include Captain Belio, if I'm not

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Mistaken?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Yes, we can proceed with Atty. Lopez and Captain Belio as manifested last week, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: What is the pleasure of Senator Judge Cayetano, Alan?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Mr. Presiding Officer, if no one objects, I will not object to having Director Matibag yesterday, but maybe as a caution to government officials, my good friend, Congressman Defensor. I read over the weekend that Director Matibag is writing because he is to be in a convention meeting the FBI next week. So actually, we're going to be here 30 weeks. We have put aside many, many important things. We have put aside many foreign trips, many local trips, whether it's to help dun sa tinamaan ng Nang lindol sa Mindanao or tinatamaan ng baha ngayon because we have to be here two o'clock until matapos tayo every Monday to Wednesday then after the sauna every Tuesday to Wednesday. I find it in bad taste that a bureau head will dictate to us that he's not available next week. I was Secretary of Foreign Affairs. That's why you have undersecretaries. That's why you have deputy director. So, I mean, I admire the patience of the prosecution, no? But even the prosecution, they have a way of timing and laying down the witnesses, eh. So, I don't want later on to say na eh dapat natanong ko muna ito sa unang witness, kaya lang si director matibag inuna dahil ganito o ganyan. I'd like to put that on record and ask my colleagues if that's acceptable to us. At least those who are not in jail or the 21 of us are here. The whole government, nakatutok. We put aside so many important things. And then one witness, who is in the government, who is a bureau head? Will tell us, sorry, but because he has to be with the FBI, siya na yung mauna tomorrow. That might be a bad precedent, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: May I be allowed to give a

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: reply? The gentleman

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: will please respond to the appoint of Senator-Judge Alan Cayetano.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: With due respect to the Honorable... Senator Judge Alan Peter Cayetano, we will always respect the decision of the honorable court. However, we will only be advancing his testimony one day based on the subpoena that we have requested the honorable court. He is scheduled to testify until Wednesday and that we will not disrupt the scheduled list of witnesses. We will simply advance it one day.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Would you respect, Congressman Representative Defensor, I ask That question poignantly last week. If Matibag will be one of your witnesses for this week and you said no. In fact, you corrected Atty. Ligutan when he mentioned Director Matibag as one of your witnesses and instead gave me a list of Lotoc, Zulaika Lopez, and Captain Belio. Matibag was not included. In fact, I don't think we issued a subpoena.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: For Director Matibag for this week, given your manifestation after you took over, given that you have, as you said, control and supervision over the private, the counsel for the prosecutors. So he's not in your list this week. He's not being advanced for a day, sir.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: May I respond, Your Honor? Please

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: so.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Your Honor, that's correct. I gave a list of witnesses scheduled for Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. However, Your Honor, to add, I also added that since NBI Director Matibag has been requested for a subpoena to testify within the week. I also added in my statement that we will inform the Honorable Court which day we can present the Honorable Matibag and I was expecting him to be presented on Wednesday after the testimony of Captain Belinda Bello, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I confirm that but the situation is Given the one-witness-per-day rule that we supposedly have under the rules of court, no subpoena has yet been issued to Director Matibag to appear this week. Can the Clerk of Court kindly confirm that for us on the record?

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: No subpoena has been issued for NBI Director Matibag.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: May I

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: respond, Your Honor? Senator Judge Alan Cayetano is recognized.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: My statement and my question to the court is not really addressed to the prosecution. You will have to do the best you can to represent what you're fighting for. So I commend you for adjusting. But my recollection is because I'm also waiting for his testimony. And my recollection last week is that we will not see him this week. And I think 11 days. 11 days ang sa article na to. So we're on day 4. So kung hindi siya pwedeng next week, that's day 7, 8, 9.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Again, I don't want to dictate sa prosecution or ano. But to suddenly say na tomorrow na siya. When I'm preparing for our oral argument tomorrow and the other witnesses, it's a

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: little bit, it's a small inconvenience for today. But I hope it doesn't become a rule, especially for a bureau head.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: I mean, if no one else objects, but if someone objects, I don't think it's really a good rule. You know, rules are important. I'll have to keep, you say technicalities, and no, rules are important. So even yung notice, we agreed on, siding officer, three day ba? Five day notice?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Five days for witnesses not mentioned in the pre-trial order. And

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: then three days kapag ka...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Three days given the fact that we will be announcing the witnesses for the following week on the last day.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Anyway, I said my piece but I hope we will not be able to move faster if we have to accommodate the witnesses especially if they're in government.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: May I add something,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Your Honor? Before the Honorable Defensor, the Presiding Officer would like to hear from the Council for the Respondents. Atty. Vinlun, what say you?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. We would have to oppose. On the basis of the following, number one, it will be in violation, your honor, of the impeachment

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: court's directive that was given last week insofar as the identities of the witnesses and as well as the order of the presentation. Number two, your honor, it will be again as mentioned by Senator Judge Cayetano, a violation of the five-day notice rule since while he was subpoenaed the week before, your honor, we are learning that

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: he will be presented this week. The five-day notice will not be observed. Number three, the prosecution cannot compel also the defense and this impeachment court to present witnesses according to their schedule, considering also that these witnesses have already been identified and determined. Of course, it will be a violation of the basic tenets of fair play. And to join again the manifestation of Senator Judge Caytana, it will set a bad precedent. And so far, surprise witnesses will be allowed at any point of the proceedings. Number five would be, it will also violate our right to cross-examine intelligently. We have done our best to prepare for

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: their witnesses. However,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: these last-minute changes really affect the preparation involved, Your Honor. And insofar as laying down the case that we want to establish and finally if there are violations of these proceeding rights there will be a violation of a

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: procedural due process which of course can give way to another ground to further delay the proceedings moreover your honor

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: um we If the prosecution would also allow, can we also get a copy, Your Honor, of that invitation? And may we inquire of the prosecution

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: if the particular travel authority has already been made? Because, Your Honor, we received information as well that

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: the FBI had already conducted a summit, a regional summit of some sort, but it was conducted of June. In June of, in other words, last month, Your Honor, also in Bangkok, Thailand. So, we would have to, again, manifest and we would have to study, Your Honor, the invitation and counter-check and do the proper verification as well. So that, if

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: it is indeed viable, then we would understand, Your Honor, why it has to be attended to by Director Matiba, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Um, Senate President Gatchalian, recognized. You may proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Thank you, thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. Sinusuportahan ko po yung statement ni Senator Judge Allen Cayetano. Dahil hindi lang naman po yung councils ng prosecution at defense na naghahanda. Pati mo mga senator judges naghahanda rin. At sa totoo lang itong weekend, marami rin sa ating mga senator judges ay pinag-aaralan kung ano yung kanilang maitatanong sa mga testigong ihaharap ngayong linggo. Marami po ay pinag-aaralan po yung mga ebedensyang inupload na para po sa ating mga senator judges. At hindi po ito konting ebedensya, pinag-uusapan po natin dito. Libo-libong mga papel at libo-libong mga ebedensya. Kung bigla pong may isisingit na testigo, hindi ho rin makakahanda po yung ating mga senator judges sa kanilang pagtatanong at hindi rin ho nilang mababasa yung mga dokumento at ebidensya na nakakabit ho doon sa testigong iharap. Kaya napakahirap naman po na naghahanda ho tayo pero biglang may mga ganitong supresya na hindi ho natin paghahandaan at hindi naman ho yan magiging maayos at For the

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: record, Chair would like to confirm the statement of the Honorable Defensor, I will quote,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We'll take for both parties. With the permission of Senators, Senator Judge Cayetano and the Senate President, may we defer our ruling on this matter and ask the Council for the Prosecution to submit to us the letter given to you by Director Matibag for us to be able to look at it. Copy furnished, of course, the Council for the Respondent so that we can adequately go over it. And hopefully come up with a ruling before the day is over.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Would that be possible?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: We will submit the letter. Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So, we shall do it that way. Kindly furnish a copy to counsel for the respondents as well for their review.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Your Honor, if the travel authority is also available, if we can ask for a copy.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Travel authority, if it's already issued.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Yes, of course. Kindly furnish us that as well. Your Honors, we will submit in good faith whatever the prosecution has received from Director Matibag, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: As well as kindly communicate with him, if possible, if he already has a travel authority for the same, so that we could evaluate it based on what you have. We cannot evaluate it based on what you don't have. So we will presume if you don't have it, it's not yet there.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, one last addition. Considering that there's a if and when they provide the travel authority, I understand, Your Honor, that one of the requirements is also the official invitation from the foreign body. So if they can also provide that, Your Honor, so that we can do a full review of this matter.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Vinluan, it's not really for the full review of the counsel for the prosecution but rather for this court's evaluation whether or not to allow the motion of the counsel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Your Honors, I respectfully request that counsel for the panel of House prosecutors, Atty. Virgil Ligutan, be recognized for the presentation of our second witness.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Ligutan, counsel for the prosecutors, is recognized to present the prosecution's second witness. You may proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Mayong hapon sa atong tanan, the second witness for the prosecution is no other than Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc. We call to the witness stand, Atty. Lotoc.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly situate Atty. Lotoc to the witness stand.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Lotoc, please remain standing as the Clerk of Court administers the oath so far as the prosecution's second witness is concerned. Clerk of Court is recognized.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Please raise your right hand. You,

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Jeremy C. Lotoc. I, Jeremy C. Lotoc.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Do swear. Do

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: swear.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: That the evidence you shall give.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: That the evidence that I will be giving. In

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: the case now pending.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: In the

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: case now pending,

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: shall be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So help

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: me

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: God.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Your witness, counsel for the prosecutors.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Atty. Lotoc, you may sit down.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Your honors, the testimony of our second witness. Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc is offered to prove the following. Number one,

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Jeremy Lotoc is a lawyer by profession and he was the chief of the Cybercrime Division of the National Bureau of Investigation, or NBI, in 2024.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: [unclear] ang dating Speaker ng House of Representatives. Pangatlo, napag-alaman ng NBI na ang mga pagbabanta ng Vice Presidente ay

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: seryoso at totoo matapos nilang isaalang-alang ang mga sumusunod Una, the manner of the respondent's delivery of the statement that she intended her remarks to be Real and serious threats. She was not merely joking when she uttered those threats.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Pangalawa, mga kababayan, even before that fateful press conference on November 23, 2024, bago yung press conference na iyan,

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: May nakontrata ng mamamatay tao yung vicepresidente bago pa man ang press conference na iyan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Pangatlo, ang utos ng vicepresidente sa asasin na huwag siyang titigil hanggat hindi napapatay ang Pangulo ng Pilipinas, ang Unang Ginang, at ang Speaker 4.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Honor,

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: basis now.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: What was your finding? Well, una, three reasons, Your Honor, if okay lang.

turns.text: Una, when the second highest official of the land openly and publicly uttered that she had already contracted a person to kill, the highest official of the land, the First Lady and the former Speaker, and that she instructed the person to be relentless in killing them, we

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: failed to see any amount of freedom of speech in that utterance, Your Honor. That's number one. Number two, we talked to ourselves.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: If we allow the argument that it is within the bounds of freedom of speech, if we allow that to become the norms of our society, then who would...

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Patayin mo si senador ganito pag itong nangyari. Patayin mo si congressman ganito pag ganito ang nangyari. Patayin mo si justice ganito pag ganito ang nangyari. So imagine, Your Honor, the anarchy, the disorder, and the chaos it would bring to our country. And number three, Your Honor, as a lawyer and being in the law enforcement, freedom of speech Protects lawful expression, but it does not protect utterances that satisfies the elements of a criminal offense. Like this one, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Satisfies the elements of a criminal offense like this one. Ito yung tanong daw, Atty.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor. Leading and calls for conclusion of law. Based

turns.text: on his investigation, let the witness answer.

turns.text: Sustained, but the Presiding Officer will ask the question to the witness.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: that would be a more complete description of what you have to comply with before you can file a case.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: We will submit, Your Honor. Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. We started the investigation on the alleged threat against the life of the Vice President.

turns.text: May nakita kami sa I think 75 PNP personnel as far as the security of the Vice President is concerned.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: 335 personnel protecting a single person, the Vice President? Based on

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: that record, Your Honor. Based on the news, yeah. 335.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Last point, Your Honor, please.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Wind up, Counsel. Yes, Your Honor. Now, Mr. Witness, you mentioned earlier that your office considered in its investigation In the November 23, 2024 online briefing, na aside kay respondent, yung vice-presidente, tsaka yung mga media personalities, okay, na nabanggit mo, sino pa, kung meron pa, yung nandun sa online briefing ngayon, kung alam mo?

turns.text: Objection vague, Your Honor.

turns.text: Oh, Your Honor, what's vague? Okay. Witness is smart enough to answer if he knows. Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: based on that video, it appears na nagko-complain si Atty. Zulaika. I'm referring doon sa paglipat niya from H.O.R. to women correction facilities, I think. And then yung health issue niya. So parang kinukomplain din niya na yun. At yung nangyari sa kanyang pagka-health in custody sa H.O.R.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: All right. Now, Atty. Lotoc, what significance, if any, do these complaints ni Atty. Lopez have in your investigation on the threats made by the Vice President in that online media briefing?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. We take that into account. Tiningnan namin 'yung sitwasyon, 'yung issue ni Atty. Zuleika. But when we see the bigger picture, taking all the pieces of the puzzle, una, it has nothing to do with the Vice President contracting a person because even before Zuleika Lopez appeared in that video, the Vice President had already contracted a person to kill the President and Liza Marcos and the former Speaker. And when we consider all the facts and circumstances, the instance where Atty. Zuleika was complaining does not diminish, it does not alter, it does not affect the totality of the findings that we have in our investigation, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Senator

At that time, Sir. Hindi ko na po alam ngayon kung sino yung mga team na, kasi nalipat na po ako sa...

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yung

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, aside from the fact, Your Honor, na nag-i-issue kami ng subpoena sa Vice President para makakuha ng information, kasi we need a validated information, we need a confirmed information. Nung in-issue namin ng subpoena yung mga media personalities, bawat isa sa

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: kanila na nag-appear, tinanong din po namin, nandoon ka ba nung sinabi ito ng Vice President? Hindi

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: ko po tinatanong kung

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: sinabi ba ito o hindi. Dahil may witness

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: rin po tayo nung nakaraang linggo na nagsabing nasabi nga ito at napanood naman natin po

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: lahat. Ang tanong ko, tinuloy niyo ba yung investigasyon para matukoy ang taong ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Unfortunately, wala akong kaming ma-establish na validated information na confirmed. In fact hanggang ngayon nag-aantay po kami. Hindi yung katulad dito sa nangyari may apparent commission of the crime dahil nandiyan yung big U eh. So ang

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: ibig niyo pong sabihin bilang NBI hindi niyo nahanap yung taong ito pero literal niyo itong sabi niyo literal itong pag-assess niyo dun sa statement dahil ito mismo yung nasabi ng Vice President.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, Your Honor, if If the second highest official of the land, sinabi yan, hindi ho biro yan. Medyo mabigat ho yan. At yung pagkasabi pa niya na may kasamang galit at mga pagmumura. We took it very seriously, Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Alright, I have a question for the defense. Sa lahat ng mga sagot ninyo, Atty. Vin Luan, parang hindi ko nakita na tinanggi ng inyong kliyente o ng depensa. Na may nakausap ang vice-presidente na tao para gawin yung mga bagay na ito. Tama ba? Wala ito sa mga sagot ninyo? We deny

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Ang nabanggit doon ay freedom of expression. Was there an exact statement there na hindi totoo?

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: We

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Okay. We'll take a look, Mr. Presiding Officer. Hanapin natin ito. And if I may come back to this once we take a look at the records, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The gentleman may do so at the appropriate time. With the permission of Senator Judge Erwin Tulfo, since nakatayo na po si Senator Judge Ejercito, ang papaunahin ko ng bumuna siya. Senator Judge Tulfo, rather Ejercito is recognized. You have two minutes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: May we know if the NBI has the authority to issue subpoena against impeachable officials? Kasi kanina po sa mga pinresent kanina, subpoena po ang inyong pinadala sa Vice President instead of a mere invitation. Yan lang po. Clarify ko lang po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Under Republic Act 10867, the NBI has authority to issue subpoena. As a matter of fact, the case involving the Vice President falls under Section 5, Paragraph G, which the NBI has primary jurisdiction to undertake investigation, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Likewise, for the information, may we know what constitutes a grave threat that will prompt the NBI to conduct an investigation as compared to a light threat? What are the elements that are needed to be present to be considered a grave threat.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, for grave threat, Your Honor, if naalala ko siya, if a person threatens another person with the infliction upon the latter's person, property, or honor, or that of the latter's family with a wrong Atty. Giorgio R. Or

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: with any wrong, amounting to a crime, if that threat is with condition or without condition or with monetary consideration, yun po yung kabuan sa grave threat.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: May kondisyon? Or walang kondisyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: The crime of grave threat, Your Honor, can be committed with or without condition. With or without

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: condition.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: So as an investigator, have you ever investigated and filed a complaint for grave threats apart from this one? Again, Your Honor? As an investigator, have you filed any case or investigated and filed a case for grave threats against anyone aside from this one, excluding this one?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: think me, nag-start po kasi ako as counter-terrorism and then organized crime group and then cybercrime.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Wala akong maalala, Your Honor, kundi ito lang. I mean, so far as my being in the NBI is concerned, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Ah, so ito lamang yung ano, ito pala yung kaso na naimbestigahan niyo concerning greed threats, yun o?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I think yung iba, may mga na-investigahan, Your Honor. Pero again, sabi ko, yung sa sarili ko po, yung experience ko from counter-terrorism hanggang sa Organized Transnational Crime Group hanggang sa Cybercrime Division, ang naalala ko lang, Your Honor, kasi matagal na ho yun eh, kung ano yung nasa record, I think itong great threats na to is, pag hindi first time, Atty. Dung ko lang na-experience.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: Gano'ng katagal kayong parte nitong Cybercrime Division? Bukay na

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: lipat? Since 2018, Your Honor. Nagsimula ako bilang Investigation Agent. And then 2022, I was designated as Chief of the Digital Forensic Laboratory Division. And then 2023, designated as Chief of the Cybercrime Division, Sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito
turns.text: So, more than five years kayong nandito sa Cybercrime Division ng NBA? Opo. That's all, Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator Judge Erick Soto. Senator Judge Tulfo Irwin is recognized. You have two minutes, sir. You may proceed when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. President or Presiding Officer. I'd like to direct my clarificatory question to the witness on the stand, Mr. Presiding Officer. Atty. Jeremy Lontoc, What findings, if any, convince the NBI the motive of the respondent to kill the President and two other people? Meron pong bang kayong nakitang motibo? Kasi maaari pong sabihin lang nung isang tao sa sobrang galit niya. Napag-usapan na po kanina yan, di ba? Spur of the moment. Pero did you find any motive? Bakit niya po gagawing patayin ang Pangulo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. As I've said before, when we take into consideration all the facts and circumstances surrounding that issue, nagkaroon ng hindi magandang relasyon yung dalawa.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Nagbato na ang vicepresidente ng mga salitang mabibigat laban sa presidente.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Pinapakita doon sa October 18 na toxic na nga yung relationship nila. Galit na galit si Sarah dahil sinasabi ng vicepresidente is politically motivated yung pag-attack sa kanya. And then at the same time, pinagtutulungan siya ng buong gobyerno. So, then na-trigger ho yun, if my memory serves me right, nung incident nangyari noong 23 November 2024.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: So parang nagpatong-patong na siya, convolution ng iba't ibang issue. So nakita ho namin, talagang galit ang Vice President sa Presidente.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, so you saw that the Vice President is very angry, right? Galit po siya. Did the investigation uncover any evidence that the respondent had taken steps to carry out these threats or these statements that she made in public and online? Did you have or did you uncover any evidence?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, insofar as the Cybercrime Division is concerned, we focused on the investigation on the alleged grave threats and inciting to sedition. Ngayon, pagdating doon whether or not merong na-execute na o may inutusan, I think ang makakasagot po niyan, Your Honor, 'yung aming Director, kasi sa kanya po 'yung pool ng information. But at the same time, 'yung jurisdiction na 'yan, nasa Intelligence Service po namin. Kami ho, nasa Investigation Service. So insofar as the NBI Cybercrime Division is concerned at that time, naka-focus po kami sa grave threats and inciting to sedition. But insofar as whether meron na bang in-engage ang Vice President, jurisdiction ho 'yan ng aming Intelligence Service, and maybe ang makakasagot niyan 'yung aming Director kasi siya po 'yung—

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: answer that because he is the recipient of a pool of information from different—

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: You

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: mean inciting to sedition will be answered by the director, is that correct? Kasi parang hindi po natalakay kanina in inciting to sedition, is it?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, Your Honor, inciting to sedition, in our investigation, we were able to establish that those utterances from 18 October 2024, November 23, 2024, and other facts and circumstances, even the November 26, 2024, we believed that those utterances have a tendency, Your Honor, to stir up the people, to go against the government, to disturb the peace of the community, and to undermine public safety and public order. I think those are the elements of inciting to sedition, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: I have two questions, Mr. Presiding Officer. So you're saying they're intertwined: killing the President and then inciting the people to revolt against the government? They're intertwined, is that what you're saying?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Based on our findings.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Based on your findings.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: What could be the motive of the vice president inciting people to sedition, to revolt against the government, when in fact she will be the next president of the republic? She's been saying and everybody knows and she's been claiming. Why do you think? Did you look deeper? Why incite to sedition?

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: In fact, you're the vice president. Usually, in our country, usually, Mr. Witness, the vice president would run for presidency. What could be the motive?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, Your Honor, what we have established is the fact that the relationship between the two were already hostile. And what we established is the fact that the vice president has committed great threats and inciting to sedition.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: That is our focus, Your Honor. Insofar as the deeper motive, I have

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: no personal knowledge. All

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: right. Well, I'm running out of time. Can you identify the strongest piece of evidence which you relied in deciding to file these cases before the Department of Justice? And what is the status of this case, Mr. Witness?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, Your Honor, the piece of evidence that we attached or we incorporated in our investigation is sufficient and has satisfied the requirements of the quantum of evidence required which is prima facie evidence. With reasonable certainty of conviction, and the fact, Your Honor, that the Department of Justice has issued certification stating that your referral, your transmittal, has complied all the elements of the crime charge and therefore good for preliminary investigation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: What is the status of the case, Mr. Witness? It's ongoing, Your Honor,

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: if I remember correctly. It's ongoing, Your Honor.

turns.text: you're the supervisor of these minutes of the meeting and you were the one who attached these documents, your affidavit of investigation. Anyway, I'll move

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: on to a new point.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: My only point is this, Mr. Lotoc. We are talking here about filing a case against the Vice President of the Philippines, who is the second-highest official of the land, and you used an unsigned document as part of your exhibits. Is that what you're trying to tell the court?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: You can ask Atty. Ria Vanessa D. Asuncion, the executive officer, kung ano ang nangyari.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, so let's go through the affidavits that were executed after the interviews. Okay, pahabol na ito lahat, tama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Kasi this was pursuant to the Feb 5 certification eh, so hinabol nyo ito lahat, tama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Hindi yung hinabol, kinumply ho namin yung requirement ng DOJ.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Ah, you want to use the term nagkinumply. Okay, sige. The interviews were in November to December 2024, but the affidavits were in February 10, 2025, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yung mga interview mismo, November to December 2024, kinundak. Pero yung mga affidavits attesting to those interviews, February of 2025 na in-execute, tama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: At any

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: rate, this was made pursuant to the Feb 5 DOJ certification, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Okay. So in short, hinanapan kayo ng DOJ ng affidavits. That's why you attach additional ones to the revised affidavit of investigation. Is that what happened?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, the affidavit was not revised. May mga attachment lang ho na nirequire yung Department of Justice. So kinumpulay ho namin. Even

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: your own director referred to it as revised, diba? So let's not make an issue about that. Exactly. I'm just asking if these were attached to the second affidavit of investigation. So, in other words, the agent who executed these affidavits were John Mark Kalilong, Gueran, and Asuncion, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And each agent executed their own affidavit, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: All were based on their personal knowledge, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, sir, based on their personal knowledge. So

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: nothing was supplied to any agent, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I don't understand the question, sir. So

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: nothing was supplied, ibig sabihin hindi binigay sa kahit anong agent yung isusulat niya doon sa affidavit. Independent nila ginawa lahat yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yung affidavit ng mga agent? Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: In other words, what you're telling this court is that these are bona fide affidavits. And not template affidavits, correct? Bonafide and not what, sir? Template. Yung hindi pinirmahan lang basta.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, I think you can ask, sir, the one who signed the affidavit, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Again, this is part of your affidavit. These are attachments to your affidavit of investigation. So you should have checked this at least, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Sa practice namin, may mga templated na talaga kung common na yung...

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Thank you. Thank you. So, in

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: other words, you use template affidavits. Let me direct your attention to the affidavit of John Mark Kalilong, pages 170 to 171, of the Articles of Impeachment's G-9. Allow me to read a portion of its paragraph. Five. It says there, no joke. Can we flash that on the screen?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: It

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: says there, no joke. No joke. Nagbili na ako.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Sige. Can we focus on that part?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, here.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yan. So, no joke, no joke. Nagbili na ako mama. Here. On the bottom portion. Nagbili na ako mama pag namatay ako. Alright? Do you confirm that there is a typographical error in the spelling of mam? Which was incorrectly spelled as mama.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Your Honor, Your Honor, with all due respect, Your Honor, please, what's the relevance of a typographical error from being mama? We will demonstrate

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: that, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I'm

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: just laying

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: the basis.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: What's the relevance? On a

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: short leash, counsel, show the connection and relevance.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Can we confirm first, your honor, if he confirms that there's a typographical error on Kalilong's affidavit?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I think since the signatories here are Agent Kalilong and Atty. Vanang Luben, sila ho ang makakasagot.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, so we cannot confirm.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So let me direct your attention to the affidavit of Geran, Agent Angely Jean Geran, pages 178 to 179 of AOI's Annex G-9. Again, let me read from paragraph 5 as well. It says here, Can we zoom that portion? No joke, no joke. Tagbiling na ako mama pag namatay ako. Do you confirm that there's also a typographical error in the spelling of the word ma'am, which was also incorrectly spelled as mama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: You can ask the one who signed this affidavit, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So you cannot confirm also?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: You can ask,

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, the one who signed it. One last.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Pages 199 to 200 of Annex G. 9 as well. This is now the affidavit of Priya Asuncion. Can I go to paragraph 5 also? No joke, no joke. Nagbili na ako, mama. Can you also confirm that there's a typographical error in the spelling of

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: mama,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: which was also incorrectly spelled as mama?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, you can ask the one who signed the affidavit. Alright, so

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: in other words, all three affidavits contain the exact typographical error of the word mama. Same paragraph number. And do you still maintain that these affidavits were independently executed?

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: Mr. Presiding Officer?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before I recognize Senator-Judge Zubiri, counsel, I think inamin naman ni Atty. Lotoc na may mga templates sila, kumbaga may mga dekahon silang affidavits. Tama ba, Atty. Lotoc?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Opo, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So posibleng isa ito sa mga dekahon ninyong affidavit? Is that possible?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Kasi same lang ho 'yung [unclear]. Siguro 'yung pag-copy-paste diyan, kung anong unang nakopy-paste doon sa [unclear], 'yun na ho 'yun.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kaya nga, kasi parehong number five, parehong [unclear], di ba? Meaning may point naman 'yung counsel for respondent. So, it's possible that isa ito sa mga dekahon ninyong affidavit?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge Zubiri, what is your pleasure, sir?

turns.speaker: Sen. Juan Miguel “Migz” F. Zubiri
turns.text: sa Bisaya pa, Your Honor, Murag Abugado. But yes, we appreciate the fastidiousness of the good counsel for the defendant on looking at all these particular issues. But due to the lateness of the hour, Your Honor, and I've been being egged by my colleagues here, we've been here for six hours, 2 to 8, 2 p.m. to 8. May we request maybe counsel for the defense or the body that we just adjourned tonight and continue tomorrow because all these details after a while I'm sure these gentlemen and ladies both for their counsel and for the prosecution has not even eaten dinner and many of them are probably tired from sitting as I am tired from sitting for six hours. May we take that break your honor and just continue tomorrow at 2 p.m. For the continuance of the impeachment court, Your Honor. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: May I know how much longer is the cross of counsel for the respondent?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Before I answer that question, Your Honor, we just manifest that this is the first time that the Vice President through counsel is confronting the witnesses against her. Of course, she did not participate during the House Committee on Justice for the reasons that were...

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Already stated in our petition for certiorari. So, to answer that question, about halfway, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We're not cutting short your time to cross-examine, counsel. We're just simply inquiring to find out if you can either simply wait for it to finish or continue tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We're okay with either, Your Honor. But to also indulge Senator Judge Subiri, we can have a continuance, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay, there being no objection on the part of counsel for respondent, given that we're cutting for tonight his cross-examination.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: One last administrative point, Your Honor. Considering the change in schedule because of the continuance, may we inquire of the prosecution if they still intend to present—

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We will get to that, counsel. We will decide on that before we adjourn. For the meantime, Court would like to excuse Atty. Lotoc with a reminder that the subpoena for him to attend tomorrow's hearing still stands and he will continue to testify under the same oath. Thank you, Your

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You are excused, Atty. Lotoc. Thank you for your time and cooperation and see you again tomorrow, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: For some administrative matters, we are in receipt of the memorandum from the Council for the Respondents with respect To the issuance of subpoena for bank records and AMLC records as well as BAR records. Do we have a similar submission from the council for the prosecutors?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly furnish clerk reports instructed to furnish all senator judges with a copy of the same with a reminder that we will be hearing the oral arguments of the parties on these two matters on Wednesday. After the presentation of the testimony of the witnesses of the Council for the Prosecution, what is the pleasure of the Honorable Defensor?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: We have no other matters to discuss, Your Honor. We will await the final ruling of the Court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The Chair would like to recognize Senate President Gatchalian.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer. Pursuant to our discussion earlier on the subpoena for NBI Director Melvin Matibag, and pursuant to the discussion with Senator-Judge Alan Cayetano and myself, and to give ample time to the senator-judges to study, to look at the pieces of evidence, as well as to propound their questions, may I propose to let him come to the Senate on Monday? I was looking at the letter from the NBI, and indeed the activity in Bangkok is quite important. It is the regional summit on scam-center compounds and transnational organized crime, which will be held on Tuesday. We were also looking at the flights to Bangkok, and there are flights at night, Mr. Presiding Officer. So what we can do is allow him to come here on Monday and then propound our questions. And if ever we don't finish it, we can request him to come back again after his activity in Bangkok.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: With the understanding, of course, Senate President Gachalian, that the testimony of the witness given in direct examination would be meaningless unless he is thoroughly cross-examined.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So, should we not finish his testimony on Monday, it shall be continued on the next trial date until the cross-examination, redirect, and if at all, recross shall have been finished by the parties. Subject to that understanding. Is there any objection to the motion of the Senate President to issue the subpoena for the attendance of Director Matibag on Monday, July 20?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: 2 o'clock in the afternoon. There being none, same is approved. Now, to clarify, the Honorable Defensor may ask, who is your witness for tomorrow? I understand we still have two witnesses online, namely Atty. Lopez and Capt. Bellio. Is that correct, sir?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: That's correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: And you will be presenting Atty. Lopez first?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Based on our earlier manifestation. We're supposed to present her next, after Law Talk, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: After the culmination of the cross, if at all, redirect and recross of Atty. Law Talk.

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you very much. Any other points that any other senator or judge would like to raise? Any other points the parties would like to raise? Counsel for Respondent, given that the Honorable Defensor already said yes. Nothing further?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We are okay with that presentation, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: There being no other matters to take up, and given the lateness of the hour, and as manifested and moved by Senator Judge Zubiri, there being no objection, the trial is hereby adjourned until 2 p.m. of Tuesday, July 14, 2026.
